key_insight: A DFT-guided all-atom model reproduces key experimental features of the resorcinol-formaldehyde aerogel skeleton and enables atomistic study of iron incorporation.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a starting point for screening fillers and dopants for RF aerogels, with potential applications in thermoelectric functionalization and thermal insulation.
method: Optimize RF base units with DFT and compare calculated infrared spectra with experiment.
Benchmark force fields against DFT for branched RF units and select COMPASS II.
Simulate skeleton aggregation and density equilibration, then track 5 wt% iron incorporation over 1 ns.
evidence_signal: The 15,012-atom model reached 1.296 g/cm³ versus an experimental skeletal density of 1.3 g/cm³; after iron addition, the embedded fraction rose from 63% to 71%.
watch_item: The branched RF units were not cross-linked to one another, and agreement with infrared spectra and skeletal density does not establish bulk thermal or thermoelectric performance.
paper_title: An All-Atom Model of the Resorcinol-Formaldehyde Aerogel Skeleton from DFT and Molecular Dynamics: Validation and Iron Incorporation
